claims.statement: The fresh production browser submits the read-only Social draft through real UI controls and the web proxy to the API, worker and database. It correlates the accepted receipt, completed run and authorized artifact, verifies mock/read-only provenance, and reloads the same artifact. No fulfilled API response or fixture backend substitutes for this live composition.

Injected-browser regressions reject broken receipt, run, artifact, provenance and reload relationships; they are not live-stack evidence. The native guard preserves Chromium security metadata, with deny-all-WebSocket mode checked by an owned canary. Existing redirect, off-origin, hierarchy, desktop/mobile and console checks remain mandatory. The complete clean-state gate supplies live delivery evidence.

The owned browser/web namespace uses a bounded loopback relay from the selected published port to the existing web listener on 8080. Raw-byte forwarding preserves browser-originated Host, Origin, Fetch Metadata and CSRF data; API trusted-origin validation and strict browser isolation are unchanged. Relay and clean-state regressions require exact origin wiring, owned lifecycle and fail-closed transport. This is origin parity, not a browser traversal of host publication.

The new delivery entrypoint serially invokes the existing complete clean-state verifier with REF=HEAD, forwards failures, and cannot silently select an older ref or replace verification with an audit or a partial suite. Restoring only Makefile to the base removes this hook and causes the retained connection tests to fail ordinarily.

Before merge approval the exact frozen candidate requires an observed complete AC-16 20-gate run and matching audit, then full committed-HEAD clean-state/browser and paired-backup gates. All existing checks, coverage, inventories, network boundaries and deadlines remain unchanged. This covers the complete constituent checks without claiming a literal make acceptance invocation.

limitations: DEL-01 adds executable delivery qualification for the existing backend/frontend, not a new API, workflow, connector or UI feature. Its injected-browser and Make-fixture controls cannot prove live execution; only the separately observed complete runs qualify the exact candidate.

The delivered target is single-operator local identity, SQLite and deterministic mocks. Optional PostgreSQL skips are not PostgreSQL qualification. Live-provider delivery, production authentication, cloud deployment, exactly-once remote effects, secure erasure and production RPO/RTO remain unqualified.

The new production UI journey exercises one read-only Social draft; it does not claim all five demos are driven through browser controls. Existing five-demo HTTP, Email approval, replay/restart, full browser inventory and other quality checks remain independently required and unfiltered.

Image/dependency acquisition may use registries. Backend/frontend test containers use network-none and browser requests use the existing scoped same-origin policy. The web ingress container retains its disclosed OS outbound route; this is not universal container egress denial or a fresh AC-15 kernel-isolation run.

The browser relay exists only in the owned shared browser/web network namespace. Its selected-port origin matches the API trust configuration, but its browser traffic does not traverse the host-published port. Existing host readiness, actual publication validation, demo and replay checks remain separate and mandatory. No HTTP header, CSRF rule, browser guard, Compose/Docker setting or verification deadline is relaxed.

The fresh 20-gate quality run plus complete clean-state and paired-backup gates cover the acceptance aggregate's constituent checks, but are not a literal make acceptance invocation. Local unsigned records prove consistency, not independently authenticated execution. CI stays disabled and all checkpoint branches are preserved.

No main merge is authorized by this manifest. Do not amend the source or commit metadata after qualification. Preserve failed candidates before replacement; keep sanitized reports and screenshots outside Git and never retain credentials, raw payloads or database/key bundles as evidence.
